caption: Measurement audit: cross-validated R² (a) and Spearman ρ (b) for predicting log₁₀ urine albumin (albumin-image features), log₁₀ urine creatinine (creatinine-image features) and log₁₀ UACR (all features). R² near 0 means no usable information.
Dose–response of four pre-specified albumin-image features across laboratory albumin bins. A monotonic trend within and across bins indicates a usable analytical response.
Within-band response of the best albumin-image feature compared with the permutation null; bars at or below the black marks are indistinguishable from chance.
Reliability and illumination sensitivity by image source: (a) ICC(1) across repeated tests (red line = filter threshold), (b) |ρ| with lux of the retained features (lower is better).

(a) Error budget: macro-F1 when albumin or creatinine is replaced by laboratory values; (b) simulated macro-F1 against the error of log₁₀ UACR, with the RMSE actually achieved by the image features (dashed lines).

Feature significance tests (all samples, descriptive): (a) volcano plot, (b) top 20 features, (c) proportion of significant features per method group, (d) agreement between ANOVA-F and mutual information.

Descriptive k-curve: sample-grouped 5-fold cross-validated macro-F1 versus the number of selected features k (feature selection is recomputed inside every fold); (a) each model, (b) cross-model mean ± SE. The k used by the final model is chosen by tuning (grid [5, 10, 20]).

Nested cross-validation (10 outer folds): (a) fold-wise macro-F1 of the five models with the two baselines (red lines); (b) mean of the six metrics; (c) mean recall per class. The MICRO column is the critical one.
Out-of-fold confusion matrices of the five models (nested CV, repeat 1; test level). Each test is predicted once by a model that never saw its sample.
Out-of-fold confusion matrices at the sample level (repeat probabilities averaged; nested CV, repeat 1).
One-vs-rest ROC curves from nested-CV out-of-fold predictions (repeat 1, test level) for the five models, and per-class F1.
Tuning stability and optimism: (a) k chosen in each of the 10 outer folds per model; (b) mean inner-CV macro-F1 (used for tuning) versus the outer-fold macro-F1 (honest estimate).
Sensitivity of the nested-CV macro-F1 of SVM (RBF) to the random division into folds. The spread across seeds is the part of the uncertainty that is due to the split alone.
Label-permutation test for SVM (RBF) (modal configuration): distribution of cross-validated macro-F1 when class labels are shuffled across samples, and the observed value.

Ablation (SVM (RBF)): (a) contribution of the information sources (albumin, creatinine, cross-image) and (b) of the quantification-method groups, measured by cross-validated macro-F1 (dotted = chance).

Feature-selection stability across the 10 outer folds: (a) frequency of the 25 most selected features for SVM (RBF) (dashed = 80 %); (b) mean pairwise Jaccard similarity of the selected sets for each model.
Permutation importance (mean ± SD over folds) of the 15 most important selected features of SVM (RBF); colour = image source (blue albumin, orange creatinine, green cross-image).
Learning curve of SVM (RBF) (sample-grouped cross-validation). A wide train–validation gap and a validation curve that is still rising indicate that additional data would help.

Error analysis of SVM (RBF) (nested-CV OOF predictions, repeat 1): (a) sample-level confusion matrix, (b) probability of the true class versus UACR, (c) model ordinal score versus laboratory UACR (dashed lines = 30 and 300 mg/g thresholds).

Calibration and the uncertain ("UNCERTAIN") zone for SVM (RBF) (nested-CV OOF repeat 1): (a) reliability diagram; (b) macro-F1 and accuracy on the accepted results versus coverage, thresholds chosen to maximise macro-F1 subject to coverage ≥ 60%; (c) share of samples of each true class that would be answered "UNCERTAIN". Exploratory: thresholds are tuned on the same out-of-fold predictions.

Final training on all samples: (a) training, tuning (inner CV) and honest (outer folds) macro-F1 of the five models; (b) ranked performance over all hyperparameter/k combinations; (c) spread per model.
Features of the deployed model (k = 10): (a) per-class z-score profile, (b) correlation among selected features (redundancy controlled by the |r| < 0.9 filter), (c) composition by group and source.
